hypothesis: The first ES move after a scheduled in-session high-impact release (FOMC decision, FOMC minutes, ISM at 10:00) partly reverses over the next two hours, so fading the W-minute reaction beats random-direction trades at the same times with the same brackets.
mechanism: Fast algorithmic reaction to headline numbers overshoots, then reverses as the full statement, presser or report is digested (overreaction/noise in announcement returns). The queued idea was to FOLLOW the move; the direction was switched to FADE in this pre-registration, before any data, because the sources below point to reversal.

sources.summary: Boguth, Fisher, Gregoire & Martineau (working paper, SSRN 4131740; read via a Scribd copy, not the SSRN original): about 60% of the market return in the four days from an FOMC announcement reverses before the next meeting; post-announcement moves look like noise or overreaction. Multi-day horizon.

Quantpedia summary of the same line of work; also mentions an E-mini 1-minute study with a ~60bp reversal lasting hours on press-conference days and none on non-presser days (secondary; original not checked).
Fordham thesis on SPY 1-minute returns in the 90 minutes after FOMC announcements, 1997-2025 (abstract only).

sources.note: Lucca & Moench pre-FOMC drift: average post-announcement return about zero (cited in the search summaries). No source found for ISM 10:00 reversals: those events are included on the general overreaction argument only, which is weaker.

closed_ideas_check: Not on CLOSED_IDEAS.md. shock_fade excluded release bars and found mild continuation for non-release shocks; this tests the excluded set with a different trigger (fixed clock times from the scheduled calendar). Intraday momentum into the close (closed) is a different window and signal. Families not in data_spend_ledger for ES.
data_caveats: news.json RTH events 2011-2021 = FOMC decision/presser/minutes (official dates) + ISM by rule (first/third business day, NOT verified), so some 10:00 'events' may be non-release days, which dilutes any effect. 2020-03-03 unscheduled cut is excluded. Event-days: dev 304, val1 113, val2 178.

rules.event: E = the earliest scheduled RTH release minute today (bar['news']); one event per session. Skip if E < 09:40 or E + W > 15:00.
rules.reference: ref = close of the 5m bar that ends at E (the bar starting E - 5); skip if that bar is missing.
rules.reaction: move = close of the bar ending at E + W minus ref, decided at that bar's close.
rules.entry: market at the next bar's open, only when flat.
rules.bracket: risk = max(|move|, MIN_RISK) points; stop at c - side*risk, target at c + side*risk (1:1 about the decision close).
rules.time_stop: exit at market after 24 completed 5m bars held (120 minutes); the engine's 15:55 flat applies first if sooner.
rules.news_filter: none beyond the event itself (a later same-day release, e.g. a 14:30 presser after a 14:00 decision, does not cancel the trade).

walk_forward: fixed: no selection; both W values are judged by the frozen dev gate and are each other's neighbour, so both must be positive for either to pass.
expected_trades_per_session: ~0.12 overall (about 1 per event-day with |move| >= 2); dev needs >= 200 trades, val >= 100, so val1 (113 event-days) is near the floor.
rejection_evidence: Reject if the frozen dev gate fails for both W. Report, not gate: the FOMC-only subset vs the ISM-only subset (the sources cover FOMC; an ISM-driven pass would not match the mechanism), and press-conference days vs others.
costs_note: risk >= 8 pts ($40 on MES); base cost ~$3.25 = <= 0.08R.
